landing_lead: A high-integrity, self-hosted SOP system for labs and small research teams — where procedures matter, but full-scale QMS software is unnecessary, expensive, or obstructive.
landing_eval_before: Evaluating? Run it with Docker and the sample data — see
landing_eval_after: . Joining your lab’s instance? Ask your admin for an invite, then sign in here.
landing_glance_sops: Versioned Markdown, immutable history, search and organization.
landing_glance_proof: Acknowledgments tied to exact published versions — not moving targets.
landing_glance_host: One stack you run yourself; content stays on disk in readable files.
landing_scope_body: From 1.0, upgrades are backup, then a new image, then an automatic database migration. sopandgo is a practical tooling aid — not a QMS, not compliance software, and not validated for regulated use. See the
landing_scope_after: for scope and the upgrade steps.
landing_fit: Built for how labs actually work
landing_fit_body: sopandgo treats SOPs as structured, versioned documents with explicit acknowledgment, auditability, and cryptographic integrity checks — while staying lightweight, transparent, and entirely self-hosted. It is for teams that need traceability without taking on a full quality management suite.
landing_simple_body: All standard operating procedures in one place. Versions are immutable and searchable. Acknowledgments are tied to exact versions — not moving targets after someone edits a file share.
landing_control_body: No cloud dependency or proprietary format lock-in. Content lives on disk as Markdown and assets you can read without the app. Style and structure procedures with Markdown, then export, back up, or migrate on your schedule.
landing_trace_body: Tamper-evident, hash-chained audit logs; SHA-256 verification for version and asset files; explicit acknowledgment tracking per version with role-based access control enforced on the server.
landing_deploy_body: Run with Docker Compose: one application image (Caddy, Go API, SvelteKit), optional Gotenberg for PDF, one published port, and one data directory. See the deployment guide for the full environment reference.
landing_security_body: The stack combines fast, stateless verification for routine API calls with server-tracked sessions so administrators can revoke access on realistic timelines. Identity stays local — invite-based onboarding, bcrypt password hashes, strict rate limits on auth endpoints, and role-based permissions evaluated only on the server.
landing_security_1: Short-lived access tokens plus refresh tokens tied to SQLite session rows.
landing_security_2: Administrative revocation within roughly five minutes via the refresh boundary.
landing_security_3: Optional SMTP delivery or manual invite links when email is not available.
landing_data_body: If the application is removed, SOP Markdown and assets remain ordinary files on disk. SQLite holds metadata, sessions, audit entries, and acknowledgments — all covered by the built-in backup export so you can validate archives and stage restores when you are ready for a controlled migration.
landing_capabilities_body: The project ships a broad slice of day-two operations work already: from authoring and PDF export to admin mail modes and staged restores. Highlights from the current README status:
landing_cap_auth: Authentication, sessions, and password reset flows
landing_cap_roles: Role-based access control for editors, readers, approvers, and admins
landing_cap_lifecycle: SOP lifecycle, Markdown editor, and asset uploads
landing_cap_audit: Audit dashboard with tamper-evident hash chains
landing_cap_mail: Mail service with SMTP or manual invite links
landing_cap_backup: Backup export, validation, and staged restore
landing_cap_pdf: PDF export via optional Gotenberg sidecar
landing_cap_word: Word import (.docx) into the draft workflow
landing_docs_body: Architecture, deployment variables, and API notes live alongside the code in the repository docs.
landing_inside_body: Product screens from the SOP library, versioned procedures, and administration tools as they appear in the application today.
